_comment: Read by scripts/build_halo.py and api/screen.js. Value floors must match on both sides or a path's verdict depends on which half an edge falls in. Fanout differs on purpose: see _rules.
_rules: Edges below the floors above are ignored, on both sides of every path. This is what stops address-poisoning dust from tainting an arbitrary wallet.
Tokens outside token_floors are ignored entirely. Spam tokens are the main dust vector.

Service nodes (exchanges, bridges, mixers, from data/services.json), contracts, and nodes above high_degree_tx_count are terminal: they can be a match but never an intermediary. Without this rule every address that has ever used Binance is three hops from Lazarus.

max_fanout_build is a compute budget, not a rule about exposure. Building the halo costs three Etherscan calls per node, so the build keeps each node's highest-value counterparties and reports its coverage. At query time the same check is a dictionary lookup and costs nothing, so max_fanout_query is set far higher: capping it would discard detections for no saving.
max_api_calls stops the build cleanly below Etherscan's 100k daily cap rather than failing mid-crawl.
